findings.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Downsize loop does not check OptimizedImage.downsize's return value, so a failed convert (exit status != 0) is silently ignored and the loop keeps retrying or proceeds with a possibly corrupt/unchanged tempfile

app/models/optimized_image.rb:141 — resize` still takes separate `width, height` while sibling `downsize` now takes a single `dimensions` string, leaving two closely related class methods with inconsistent call conventions for the same concept
app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — rescue nil` swallows all download errors (timeouts, network failures, non-image content) with no logging, making failures silent and undiagnosable

app/models/optimized_image.rb:161 — convert_with` shells out via backtick interpolation with no process timeout, so a hung/slow ImageMagick invocation (e.g. large or malicious image) can block indefinitely

app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — Hardcoding tempfile = FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) ignores the admin-configured SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, silently overriding an operator-controlled resource/abuse limit for API-driven remote URL fetches

goldens.comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.

Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).

Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:66 — Downsize loop does not check OptimizedImage.downsize's return value, so a failed convert (exit status != 0) is silently ignored and the loop keeps retrying or proceeds with a possibly corrupt/unchanged tempfile

adjudication.rationale: In uploads_controller.rb the new downsizing loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` but ignores its result. In optimized_image.rb, `downsize` -> `optimize` -> `convert_with`, and `convert_with` explicitly returns `false` when the convert command fails (`$?.exitstatus != 0`). Because the loop doesn’t check that return value (or otherwise detect failure), a failed convert is silently ignored and the code may retry pointlessly and/or proceed to `Upload.create_for(...)` with an unchanged (still-oversize) tempfile, undermining the intended “auto-reduce” behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:141 — resize` still takes separate `width, height` while sibling `downsize` now takes a single `dimensions` string, leaving two closely related class methods with inconsistent call conventions for the same concept

adjudication.rationale: In `app/models/optimized_image.rb`, `resize(from, to, width, height, opts={})` still accepts separate `width, height` and now internally formats them into a single dimensions string (`"#{width}x#{height}"`) passed to `optimize`. Meanwhile, `downsize` ends up defined with a different public signature (`downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`) that takes a preformatted dimensions string. This creates an inconsistency in the public API between two closely related operations (one takes width/height, the other takes a dimensions string), which is a real, diff-grounded review concern but not a directly verifiable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — rescue nil` swallows all download errors (timeouts, network failures, non-image content) with no logging, making failures silent and undiagnosable

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `tempfile = FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) rescue nil`, which rescues all exceptions and returns `nil` without any logging. If the download fails, `tempfile` can be `nil`, and later the code calls `tempfile.size` when creating the upload (`Upload.create_for(... tempfile.size, ...)`), which would raise `NoMethodError` and makes the root cause (download error) silent/undiagnosable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/models/optimized_image.rb:161 — convert_with` shells out via backtick interpolation with no process timeout, so a hung/slow ImageMagick invocation (e.g. large or malicious image) can block indefinitely

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new upload-time loop in `uploads_controller.rb` that repeatedly calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(...)` on user-supplied images. `OptimizedImage.convert_with` still executes ImageMagick via backticks (`` `#{instructions.join(" ")} &> /dev/null` ``) with no timeout or other guard, so a hung/slow conversion can block the request thread indefinitely. While `convert_with` itself isn’t modified here, the new downsizing path increases exposure to untrusted inputs and makes the lack of a timeout a real, diff-exposed availability defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/controllers/uploads_controller.rb:55 — Hardcoding tempfile = FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...) ignores the admin-configured SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb, silently overriding an operator-controlled resource/abuse limit for API-driven remote URL fetches

adjudication.rationale: The diff does replace the API URL download cap from `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` to a fixed `10.megabytes` in `uploads_controller.rb` (line shown in the diff). This does mean the remote fetch limit is no longer operator-configurable via that setting. However, the change appears intentional and consistent with other parts of the diff hardcoding a 10MB client/error limit, while still enforcing `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb` later via the new downsize loop before creating the upload. So it’s a real, diff-grounded configuration/abuse-limit concern, but not a clearly verifiable defect on its own.
